metadata.title: SSO callback redirect to /admin makes platform_viewer users unable to use SSO login
metadata.author: adarak14

description:
## Summary

After a successful SSO login (any provider), the callback handler in
`mcpgateway/routers/sso.py` unconditionally redirects the browser to
`{root_path}/admin`. The `AdminAuthMiddleware` then requires the user to either
be `is_admin = true` or to have an `admin.*` permission resolved through a
`?team_id=...` query parameter. Because the redirect contains no `team_id`,
**non-platform-admin SSO users are immediately bounced back to
`/admin/login?error=admin_required`** with the message *"Admin privileges
required"*, even when they have legitimate team-scoped roles and access to
non-admin parts of the platform.

This effectively means SSO login is **only practical for users who are
platform-admins**. Any deployment that wants to let regular employees log in via
SSO and use the platform as a `platform_viewer` (or as a team-scoped
`team_admin`) cannot do so with the current implementation.

## Affects

- v1.0.0 (verified)
- main (verified)
- All SSO providers — the callback is shared (`okta`, `google`, `github`,
  `keycloak`, `entra`, `adfs`, **`generic`**). Switching to the generic OIDC
  provider does not work around it.

## Reproduction

1. Configure any SSO provider (e.g. `SSO_OKTA_ENABLED=true`).
2. Set `SSO_AUTO_CREATE_USERS=true`, `SSO_TRUSTED_DOMAINS=["yourcompany.com"]`.
3. Do **not** add the test user to `SSO_AUTO_ADMIN_DOMAINS` (or any
   provider-specific admin group/domain list).
4. Optionally configure a team mapping (e.g. `OKTA_GROUP_MAPPING`) so the user is
   added to a team with role `member` (default).
5. Click "Continue with <Provider>" on `/admin/login` and complete the OIDC flow.

**Expected:** Either the user lands somewhere usable (e.g. their team's view,
the user-facing portion of the platform, or `/admin/?team_id=...` if they have
any team-scoped `admin.*` permission).

**Actual:** Browser is redirected to `/admin`, `AdminAuthMiddleware` evaluates
`has_admin_permission(email, team_id=None, token_teams=token_teams)` which
returns `False` for users without `is_admin = true`, and the user is bounced to
`/admin/login?error=admin_required`.

## Code references

The hardcoded post-callback redirect (no `team_id` ever provided):

```python
# mcpgateway/routers/sso.py — v1.0.0, around line 400
redirect_response = RedirectResponse(url=f"{root_path}/admin", status_code=302)
```

The middleware that 403s:

```python
# mcpgateway/main.py — AdminAuthMiddleware, around line 2618
return self._error_response(request, root_path, 403,
    "Admin privileges required", "admin_required")
```

The team-scoped fallback that is *never reached* from the SSO redirect because
`team_id` is missing:

```python
# mcpgateway/services/permission_service.py — has_admin_permission
# When team_id is provided, this includes team-scoped roles for that team,
# allowing team members with admin.dashboard to access the admin UI in their
# team context.
```

## Suggested fix (any of these would unblock the use case)

1. **Land non-admin users on a team-scoped URL.** In the SSO callback, if the
   newly authenticated user has at least one team membership (via
   `team_mapping` or otherwise), append `?team_id=<first_team_id>` to the
   redirect when the user is not a platform admin. Then the existing
   `has_admin_permission(..., team_id=...)` path can grant access if the user
   has any `admin.*` permission for that team.

2. **Configurable post-SSO destination.** Add an env var
   `SSO_POST_LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL` (default: `/admin`) so operators can route
   regular users to a non-admin page if their deployment provides one. This
   also avoids the assumption that every authenticated user is an admin.

3. **Add an explicit `is_admin` branch in the redirect:** when the user is a
   platform admin → `/admin`; otherwise → `/` (or some user-facing route).

The first option is the most backwards-compatible; the second is the most
flexible.

## Related observation: no Okta-specific admin groups env var

While debugging this, we noticed there is no `SSO_OKTA_ADMIN_GROUPS` env var
mirroring `SSO_ENTRA_ADMIN_GROUPS` or `SSO_GENERIC_ADMIN_GROUPS`. The only
documented path for SSO-driven admin promotion for an Okta-managed tenant is
`SSO_AUTO_ADMIN_DOMAINS`, which is domain-based, not group-based. We can
populate `provider_metadata.admin_groups` directly in the database (and the
bootstrap smart-merge preserves it across restarts), but this is not
documented. If there is appetite for it, a follow-up PR adding
`SSO_OKTA_ADMIN_GROUPS` (and exposing it via `provider_metadata` in the Okta
bootstrap, similar to the Generic OIDC provider) would close the loop.

## Environment

- Context Forge v1.0.0 (also verified on `main`)
- Deployment: Helm chart (`mcp-stack`) on AWS EKS
- SSO provider: Okta (also affects other providers per code review)

comments.author: bogdanmariusc10
comments.body:
Thank you for the detailed report, @adarak14 ! I've verified this issue exists in both v1.0.0 and main.

### Root Cause

The SSO callback handler unconditionally redirects all authenticated users to `/admin` without any `team_id` parameter:

**[`mcpgateway/routers/sso.py:402`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/routers/sso.py#L402)**
```python
redirect_response = RedirectResponse(url=f"{root_path}/admin", status_code=302)
```

The `AdminAuthMiddleware` then evaluates admin permissions, but without a `team_id` in the URL, it cannot resolve team-scoped `admin.*` permissions. The middleware checks:

**[`mcpgateway/main.py:2764-2771`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/main.py#L2764-L2771)**
```python
has_admin_access = await permission_service.has_admin_permission(
    auth_user_email,
    team_id=validated_team_id,  # This is None from SSO redirect
    token_teams=token_teams,
)
```

The `has_admin_permission` method is designed to support team-scoped admin access, but only when `team_id` is provided:

**[`mcpgateway/services/permission_service.py:202-205`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/permission_service.py#L202-L205)**
```python
# When team_id is provided, this includes team-scoped roles for
# that team, allowing team members with admin.dashboard to access
# the admin UI in their team context.
user_permissions = await self.get_user_permissions(user_email, team_id=team_id, ...)
```

### Impact Confirmed

- ✅ **Platform admins** (`is_admin=true`): Can use SSO login
- ❌ **Team admins** with `admin.*` permissions: Blocked (no `team_id` in redirect)
- ❌ **Regular users** (`platform_viewer`, `developer`, etc.): Blocked
- ❌ **All SSO providers affected**: Okta, Google, GitHub, Keycloak, Entra, ADFS, Generic OIDC

### Your Suggested Fixes

Your **Option 1** (land non-admin users on team-scoped URL) is the most backwards-compatible approach. The infrastructure is already in place:

1. SSO creates session tokens with server-side team resolution ([`sso_service.py:2128`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/sso_service.py#L2128))
2. Team mappings are applied during SSO authentication ([`sso_service.py:2053`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/sso_service.py#L2053))
3. User teams can be retrieved via `TeamManagementService.get_user_teams()` ([`team_management_service.py:1040`](https://github.com/contextforge/mcp-context-forge/blob/main/mcpgateway/services/team_management_service.py#L1040))

The fix would be to modify the SSO callback to:
1. Check if user is platform admin
2. If not, retrieve user's teams
3. If user has teams, redirect to `/admin?team_id=<first_team_id>`
4. Otherwise, redirect to `/` or a configurable landing page

**Option 2** (configurable post-SSO destination) is also worth considering for maximum flexibility.

### Additional Finding: Okta Admin Groups

Your observation about the missing `SSO_OKTA_ADMIN_GROUPS` environment variable is correct. Unlike Entra (`SSO_ENTRA_ADMIN_GROUPS`) and Generic OIDC (`SSO_GENERIC_ADMIN_GROUPS`), Okta only supports domain-based admin promotion via `SSO_AUTO_ADMIN_DOMAINS`. This forces operators to either:
- Use domain-based matching (less granular)
- Manually configure `provider_metadata.admin_groups` in the database (undocumented)

Adding `SSO_OKTA_ADMIN_GROUPS` would provide feature parity with other providers.

### **I recommend you to open a feature report for this particular finding.**

### **I will open a PR for this fix.**
